title: Discovery of a 13-Sharpe OOS Factor: Drift Regimes Unlock Hidden Cross-Sectional Predictability

extraction.methodology_summary: The strategy combines an un-levered cross-sectional value score and a short-term reversal z-score, multiplied by a binary stock-specific regime gate based on whether a stock exhibits positive daily returns on over 60% of trailing 63 trading days. Portfolios are constructed daily as market-neutral long-short with constant gross exposure of 100%, and tested using a walk-forward framework across three distinct test windows (2010-2011, 2015-2016, 2020-2021) with frozen parameters.

performance_metrics.evidence_quote: combined Sharpe ratio of 13.19, annualized returns of 158.6%, volatility of 12.0%, and maximum drawdown of −11.9%

key_findings: Regime-conditional signal activation based on stock-specific drift conditions unlocks high out-of-sample risk-adjusted performance with a combined Sharpe ratio of 13.19 across a 20-year walk-forward test framework.
Traditional risk factors (Fama-French and momentum) fail to explain returns, collectively accounting for less than 3% of total R-squared variance.
The strategy exhibits strong resilience during extreme market stress, maintaining a Sharpe ratio of 4.1 under simulated 2008 liquidity crisis conditions.
Conservative capacity analysis estimates deployable capital between $100 million and $500 million before material performance degradation occurs.
limitations: Survivorship bias is introduced by using current constituents of the S&P 500.
Strategy path dependency relies on the presence of drift regimes, leading to minimal returns during extended non-drift periods.
Real-world constraints such as short-selling limits, regulatory changes, and execution frictions could reduce realized performance.
